Authoring Tools

Editor & Wings Assembler

The editor is your workspace for building, testing, and iterating on game content.

Main Modes

  • World Mode — Edit the live scene, place assets, and test gameplay.
  • Wings Assembler — Dedicated workspace for building reusable Fragment hierarchies.
  • Material Editor — Create and edit appearance assets.

Content Browser

Browse Meshes, Materials, and Fragments. Create new content and add to world or assembler.

The current editor-camera X, Y, and Z coordinates are shown centered along the top edge of the Content Browser, keeping the readout out of the way of other editors.

Wings Assembler

Build modular assemblies with mesh nodes, empty pivots, transforms, and material assignments. Save as FragmentAsset.

The ? beside the Wings Assembler heading opens this reference from the editor.

Hierarchy & Details

Inspect and edit selected actors, components, and transform values.

Wings Assembler Details

Wings Assembler stores the Fragment's reusable hierarchy and its authored ComponentDefinitions. The Details panel is intentionally compact; use this section for the ownership rules behind those controls.

Authoring areaRuntime meaning
Root > Core ComponentsShared definitions. They are applied to authored instances using None, Player, or AI.
Behavior Profiles > Player / AIDefinitions for only the selected controller profile.
Behavior Profiles > NoneInert profile selection; it is not a shared-components bucket. Only Core Components run for Controller: None.
Anchor ComponentsLocalized behavior attached to an Anchor's world pose and active Fragment context.
Mesh Data RootShared mesh presentation bindings. Mesh Parts inherit them and do not own gameplay components.

Place a component in Core only when the same definition should exist for every controller context. For example, shared Targeting, Weapon, Acceleration, Pitch, Yaw, or Barrel Roll definitions can keep Player, AI, and future commander profiles cleaner. Auto Combat and Auto Input can also be shared when every controller should use them. Keep hardware bindings in the Player Input Manager; AI commanders provide the same logical input channels through their own producers.

Root Physical Collider

Capsule and Compound Capsule are movable kinematic bodies. Convex is a baked precise body, while Complex As Simple uses structural mesh triangles. Visibility changes only the diagnostic wireframe; it never changes collision.

For a capsule, Half Height is the center-to-cap distance. Setting Half Height equal to Radius produces a spherical capsule. Compound Capsule combines up to four capsule shapes into one Fragment body.

Global Environment

The World has one authorable Global Reflection Environment. Its rotation changes the current reflection environment; translation is editor positioning, and scale is reserved for future local reflection volumes. The environment remains selectable for its Details controls, but its viewport gizmo is hidden to keep the environment view clear.

SystemMeaning
Primary Directional LightDirect illumination only. It does not change the visible background or reflection environment.
Sky LightOpposite-direction fill using the inverse Primary Directional Light direction. It lights metal and non-metal surfaces without changing the visible background or reflection environment.
Static Space BackgroundVisible backdrop only. It does not change reflections or lighting.
Celestial PresentationCelestial features are authored in the separate Celestial Presentation workspace.

Use the ? button beside Global Reflection Environment in Details to return to this reference.

Game Viewport Settings

Gameplay Resolution owns the logical gameplay composition, camera aspect, physical presentation rectangle, input bounds, and crosshair placement. UI Resolution owns only the logical Wings UI canvas and layout; the UI still renders inside the same physical gameplay rectangle.

Render Scale remains separate: it changes only the internal 3D HDR/depth/bloom pixel cost, never UI anchors, touch bounds, or gameplay composition.

Landscape and Portrait pairs can be linked while editing. The link preserves orientation: Landscape Width maps to Portrait Height, and Landscape Height maps to Portrait Width. The link is an editor convenience and is not saved as runtime project data.

Resolution presets are 640×360, 960×540, 1280×720, and 1920×1080. Manual values remain valid and display as Custom.

World Topology

Periodic World Rendering is visual-only. One bounded arena is presented continuously through translated neighboring copies; gameplay actors and simulation remain singular. The static celestial sky remains direction-only and never wraps.

Arena Cube Size defines the authored arena. Wrapped World Scale defines the larger presentation cube as a percentage of that arena. Debug cube controls are editor-session diagnostics only and do not affect collision, packaged gameplay, or project content.

Play / Stop

Test your scene with full gameplay simulation. Play clears the previous editor world-item selection so it cannot look like a gameplay target; Stop returns to the authored state.

Fragment Camera Spring Arm

A Camera node inside a Fragment may use a Spring Arm for a smoothed third-person follow pose. The Camera node remains the authored rig and pivot; the Spring Arm resolves its final position, look target, and lag.

SettingResult
Follow Ship Up: OffUses a stable world-up reference, keeping the horizon readable while the ship rolls or loops.
Follow Ship Up: OnUses the authored Camera node’s local +Z up direction, so the gameplay camera rolls with the ship and keeps the ship’s top toward the top of the view.

Follow Ship Up is saved on the Camera node’s Spring Arm. It is off by default. It affects Spring Arm cameras only; a Camera without a Spring Arm already uses its authored world transform and up direction directly.

Placed Fragment Preview

World Mode previews a placed Fragment using its assigned Team materials and Agent Binding, so the editor viewport matches the presentation used when Play starts.

Team colors apply to mesh materials authored with the Team Color or Team Emissive channel role. Fixed materials keep their authored appearance. Assigning Day or Night applies that team’s canonical heading; the saved base rotation offset preserves additional authored rotation afterward.

Gameplay Role Base marks a lane origin. You can use multiple Base buildings for Day and multiple Base buildings for Night; matching roots pair by authoring order to create parallel lane pushes. Use Gameplay Role None for additional buildings that should not be lane origins. Once Agent Binding is Day or Night, Align To Agent appears directly below it and restores that Fragment’s deterministic heading.

Empty Actor Agents

An Empty Actor can author a logical Agent. In its Details panel, set Gameplay Role to Agent, then configure Agent Id, Team, Bot, Starting Resources, Income, Unit Cap, and Kill Reward.

When Play starts, the scene-authored Agent is created through the same runtime Agent system used by WingScript CreateAgent(...). The Empty Actor’s position, rotation, and scale are ignored for Agent gameplay, so place the authoring host anywhere convenient in the hierarchy.

Leave Gameplay Role as None for an ordinary Empty Actor. WingScript CreateAgent(...) remains supported for runtime-created or scripted Agents. If both systems use the same Agent Id, the scene-authored definition wins for that Play session.

Key Workflow

Content Browser → Wings Assembler → Save Fragment → Place in World → Play to test.
